categories.main_business_segments: C.H. Robinson operates two primary reportable segments: North American Surface Transportation (NAST), which provides truckload and less-than-truckload (LTL) transportation and logistics services across North America, and Global Forwarding, which offers ocean, air, and customs brokerage services worldwide. The All Other and Corporate segment includes Robinson Fresh (sourcing and marketing of fresh produce), Managed Solutions (3PL/4PL and TMS services), and other surface transportation outside North America. The company recently divested its Europe Surface Transportation business, completed in early 2025.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages its proprietary Navisphere platform, a global multimodal transportation management system, to connect customers and carriers, optimize shipments, and provide real-time visibility and analytics. C.H. Robinson invests heavily in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data science to automate processes, enhance dynamic pricing and costing models, and deliver advanced supply chain solutions. Its technology suite includes tools like Navisphere Insight, Navisphere Optimizer, Procure IQ, and Emissions IQ, supporting both operational efficiency and customer-facing innovation.
categories.primary_customers_markets: C.H. Robinson serves approximately 83,000 customers globally, ranging from Fortune 100 companies to small businesses, across a wide variety of industries including retail, food and beverage, manufacturing, automotive, technology, and consumer goods. Its Robinson Fresh division targets grocery retailers, restaurants, foodservice distributors, and produce wholesalers. The company’s largest customer accounts for about 2% of total revenues, with the top 100 customers representing roughly a third of consolidated revenues.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates in North America, Europe, Asia, Oceania, South America, and the Middle East, with a network of approximately 210 offices in 36 countries and 13,781 employees in 38 countries. While the U.S. remains its largest market, C.H. Robinson has significant operations and customer bases in other regions, and its Global Forwarding segment provides international logistics services worldwide. The company recently exited its Europe Surface Transportation business.
categories.supply_chain_position: C.H. Robinson acts primarily as a third-party logistics (3PL) and fourth-party logistics (4PL) provider, operating as an intermediary between shippers and a vast network of over 450,000 contracted transportation providers (carriers, railroads, ocean and air carriers). The company does not own significant transportation assets, positioning itself midstream in the supply chain, orchestrating and optimizing freight movement and supply chain solutions for its customers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, C.H. Robinson is focused on digital transformation, operational efficiency, and expanding its technology-driven logistics platform. Key R&D initiatives include the development and deployment of AI, machine learning, and data analytics to automate and optimize logistics processes, enhance dynamic pricing, and deliver sustainability solutions. The company prioritizes continuous improvement, customer-centric innovation, and expanding its integrated suite of global logistics services, while divesting non-core assets to focus on core growth engines.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through the arrangement of transportation and logistics services, charging customers for freight movement and related value-added services, and paying transportation providers for capacity. Revenue is recognized as services are rendered, typically over the transit period. In its sourcing business, revenue comes from the buying and selling of fresh produce. Additional revenue streams include fee-based managed solutions, warehousing, customs brokerage, and supply chain consulting.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: C.H. Robinson competes in a highly fragmented and competitive logistics industry against traditional asset-based carriers, other 3PLs and 4PLs, technology-enabled freight brokers, NVOCCs, IACs, and digital freight platforms. Major competitors include XPO, Expeditors, Kuehne + Nagel, DHL, and digital disruptors like Uber Freight and Convoy. The company is positioned as one of the largest global logistics platforms, emphasizing its scale, technology, data assets, and integrated service offering as key differentiators.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, C.H. Robinson reported total revenues of $17.7 billion and net income of $466 million, with adjusted gross profits of $2.8 billion and an adjusted operating margin of 24.2%. The company experienced modest revenue growth (0.7%) year-over-year, with stronger growth in adjusted gross profit (6.2%) and net income (43%). The business is cash-generative, maintains a strong balance sheet, and continues to invest in technology and global expansion while optimizing its cost structure.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: C.H. Robinson differentiates itself through its scale, global reach, proprietary technology platform, and deep data assets, enabling it to deliver tailored, integrated logistics solutions and exceptional customer service. Its value proposition centers on providing reliable capacity, advanced visibility, data-driven insights, and cost savings to customers navigating complex supply chains. The company emphasizes its people, technology, and process expertise as key drivers of customer success and competitive advantage.
